title: Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack — Release Checklist + Comms Draft (v0.9)
content:
Doc intent
- Single place to run release readiness for the “Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack” and draft the comms to: eng-oncall, SRE, Support/CS, and Release Train.
- This is intentionally operational (checklists + templates). Deeper technical background lives in Confluence.

Release identification (fill-in)
- Runtime release train: runtime-1.18.0 (target) / runtime-1.18.x (backport optional)
- Profile pack version: profiles-2025.12.0
- Included SKUs: H100 (default), L40S (default), B200 (experimental gated)
- Deployment modes: Hosted ✅, Dedicated ✅, Private ✅ (Helm wiring required)
- Rollout window: Tue–Thu, 10:00–16:00 PT (avoid weekend handoffs)

Scope reminder (what we are/aren’t promising)
- We are shipping versioned configs + runtime selection/override logic + dashboards/gates.
- We are NOT promising universally lower latency; profiles have workload envelopes and may trade throughput vs tail latency depending on preset.
- “Expected behavior” wording only. No SLA/guarantee language in docs or comms.


1) Sign-offs (must be explicit before enabling outside canary pools)
Owner: Talia Benson

A) Engineering sign-off
[ ] Runtime Kernels: Hiro Tanaka (or delegate: Grace Kim / Yuki Sato / Isabella Rossi)
[ ] Runtime Scheduling: Sofia Ivanova (or delegate: Lena Fischer / Marcus Reed)
[ ] Config/Guardrails: Ethan Park + Benji Okafor
[ ] Benchmark methodology: Claire Dubois
[ ] Benchmark harness: Rina Kobayashi

B) Infra/SRE sign-off
[ ] Fleet rollout: Irene Choi + Vanessa Ortiz
[ ] SRE sponsor: Neha Kapoor
[ ] Oncall readiness: Sean Gallagher
[ ] Alerting standards review: Allison Grant

C) Product/Docs sign-off
[ ] Rollout/rollback UX alignment: Marissa Cole
[ ] Canary/rollback requirements: Paula Mendes
[ ] Docs program: Elliot Price
[ ] Runbook/operator docs: Kira Thompson

D) Release train sign-off
[ ] Release train owner: Connor O’Brien (ship vehicle + backport decision)


2) Pre-merge / pre-release readiness checklist
2.1 Code & schema readiness
[ ] Profile schema merged + validation tests green (ref: PR-21984)
[ ] Runtime loader + override order merged (ref: PR-21991)
[ ] Integration tests for precedence/rollback toggles green (ref: PR-22047)
[ ] Startup logs include compatibility matrix for runtime/profile versioning (ref: PR-22041)
[ ] CLI/tool exists to dump effective runtime config (ref: PR-22066) and instructions included in runbook
[ ] Helm chart values documented for Dedicated/Private overrides (ref: redwood-helm-charts/pr-612)

2.2 Observability readiness
[ ] Metrics emitted: selected_profile, override_source, profile_version, key knob values (ref: PR-22027)
[ ] Dashboard panels exist for profile segmentation + tail latency (ref: observability-pack/pr-488)
[ ] Perf-canary gates merged + routing set (ref: perf-canary/pr-731)
[ ] Alert routes verified: #eng-oncall, #eng-sre, #eng-runtime (and paging policy confirmed)

2.3 Docs readiness
[ ] “Expected behavior” docs updated (H100/L40S/B200) + links shared with SRE/Support (ref: redwood-docs/pr-903)
[ ] Runbook updated with:
    - how to disable profiles per pool
    - how to force baseline defaults
    - how to confirm effective config
    - rollback thresholds

2.4 Compatibility & guardrails
[ ] GPU SKU detection normalization reviewed against known provider variants (see Slack: eng-infra “gpu sku string variants”)
[ ] MIG + multi-GPU node behavior documented (what applies per-device vs per-node)
[ ] B200 gating:
    - behind feature flag
    - version checks for driver/CUDA
    - explicit fallback behavior to H100-like baseline or safe-default profile


3) Benchmarks & acceptance criteria (what must be green)
Owner: Claire Dubois / Rina Kobayashi

3.1 Benchmark artifacts produced for each SKU
[ ] H100 baseline vs tuned curves attached
[ ] L40S baseline vs tuned curves attached
[ ] B200 exploratory curves attached (mark “experimental / limited fleet access”)

3.2 Acceptance criteria (release-blocking)
- Note: we use “no worse than” gates for safety. We can accept small p50 wins with flat p95, but cannot ship meaningful p95 regressions.

Hosted/Dedicated common gates (profile-enabled build vs baseline build)
[ ] Error rate: +0.00% absolute increase beyond noise (block if sustained)
[ ] OOM / CUDA OOM: must not increase (block if any reproducible increase in standard matrix)
[ ] p95 end-to-end latency: must be within +5% at matched concurrency for supported workload buckets
[ ] p99 end-to-end latency: must be within +8% for supported workload buckets
[ ] Tokens/sec/GPU (decode-heavy): must be >= baseline -2% (block if worse unless justified + pre-approved)
[ ] Streaming stability: no increase in stream resets / chunk timeouts
[ ] Queueing/backpressure: no sustained queue growth under target QPS envelope

Per-SKU notes
- H100: balanced preset should improve throughput at moderate concurrency; we must watch prefill/decode fairness p95.
- L40S: primary objective is stability and OOM prevention. Throughput wins are nice-to-have.
- B200: ship behind experimental gating only; do not default-enable outside explicitly approved pools.


4) Dashboards that must be green (links TBD by Aisha / Allison)
Owner: Aisha Bello

Required dashboards (minimum)
[ ] Runtime Overview (by pool/region) — error rate, request rate, saturation
[ ] Latency (p50/p95/p99) segmented by selected_profile
[ ] Throughput — tokens/sec/GPU segmented by selected_profile
[ ] GPU Memory/KV Cache — reserved, used, fragmentation proxy, eviction rate
[ ] Scheduler Health — queue depth, backpressure events, admission drops, prefill/decode split
[ ] Profile Selection Health — percent unknown SKU, percent fallback-to-safe-default, override_source breakdown

Hard “stop/rollback” thresholds during rollout (applies for >= 15 min and confirmed not due to upstream)
[ ] p95 latency regression > 10% in canary pool vs control pool
[ ] p99 latency regression > 15%
[ ] Error rate increase > 0.2% absolute
[ ] Any increase in OOMs above baseline
[ ] Any sustained unknown-SKU profile selection > 1% of traffic


5) Rollout plan (high level; detailed steps in Confluence runbook)
Owner: Irene Choi / Sean Gallagher

5.1 Rollout ordering
Phase 0: internal perf-canary + CI gates (no customer traffic)
Phase 1: Hosted canary pools (single region) — H100 only
Phase 2: Hosted multi-region (H100) + small L40S pool
Phase 3: Dedicated default-on for new pools only (existing pools opt-in)
Phase 4: Private availability (documentation + Helm values; default remains baseline unless customer opts in)
Phase 5: B200 experimental (explicitly approved pools only)

5.2 Control vs treatment
- Maintain a control pool per SKU where baseline defaults stay enabled.
- Ensure routing can quickly shift traffic back to control pool.

5.3 Rollback mechanism (must be practiced)
[ ] Verified kill switch: disable profile pack per pool (config service / env var / Helm value)
[ ] Verified ability to pin a specific profile version (e.g., profiles-2025.11.2)
[ ] Verified runtime fallback behavior when profile is invalid/unsupported (safe defaults + explicit logs)
[ ] Verified oncall can confirm effective config via debug endpoint / CLI dump


6) Release day checklist (operator view)
T-24h
[ ] Confirm release notes draft is ready (internal)
[ ] Confirm dashboards + alerts working in canary environment
[ ] Confirm canary pools have “control” routing available
[ ] Confirm Support + CS heads-up scheduled

T-2h
[ ] All sign-offs collected (Section 1)
[ ] Perf-canary results posted in #eng-runtime
[ ] Confirm no major incidents ongoing in target regions/pools

T-0
[ ] Enable profiles in canary pool(s)
[ ] Start rollout log thread in #eng-runtime and tag #eng-oncall
[ ] Post initial “expected behavior + rollback” summary (template below)

T+30m
[ ] Check stop/rollback thresholds
[ ] Validate profile selection metrics show expected skew (H100 chosen, minimal fallback)

T+2h
[ ] If stable, proceed to next phase
[ ] If unstable, rollback and open incident/retro ticket

T+24h
[ ] Post postmortem-lite summary if any rollback or near-miss
[ ] Record final deltas in benchmark report + update known issues


7) Comms templates
7.1 #eng-oncall heads-up (short)
Subject: Heads-up: enabling Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack (H100/L40S) — rollback ready

Message:
Today between <start–end PT>, we’re enabling the Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack (profiles-2025.12.0) in <pool/region>.

What changes:
- Runtime will select a per-SKU tuned config (H100 default-on; L40S default-on in selected pools; B200 remains experimental + gated).

What to watch:
- Latency (p95/p99) and error rate segmented by selected_profile
- OOM/CUDA OOM, queue depth/backpressure events

Rollback:
- Kill switch: <how to disable per pool> (see runbook)
- If you need help, tag @eng-runtime-oncall and link the dashboard snapshot.

Links:
- Runbook: <confluence link>
- Dashboards: <grafana links>
- Debug: effective config dump command: <command/link>

7.2 #customer-support / #customer-success heads-up (plain language)
Subject: Runtime change: hardware-based tuning profiles (expected improvements; opt-out available)

Message:
We’re rolling out a runtime update that applies “hardware tuning profiles” on supported GPU types. This is intended to improve or stabilize throughput/cost and reduce mis-tuned settings.

Important notes:
- This is not a product/API change. Behavior is workload-dependent; we describe “expected behavior,” not guarantees.
- If a customer reports a regression (latency spike / timeouts), Support can request a pool-level rollback immediately.

Triage checklist (Support-facing):
1) Ask for: deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), region/pool, model, request type (streaming vs non), typical prompt/output sizes.
2) Check: whether selected_profile changed around the reported time.
3) If severe: request rollback to baseline defaults for that pool.
4) Attach: dashboard screenshot + timestamps.

Support macro snippet (copy/paste)
“We recently enabled hardware-specific runtime tuning profiles in your environment to improve performance and stability. In rare cases, certain workloads can see higher tail latency. We can disable the profile for your pool while we investigate. Could you share the approximate timestamps, region, model, and whether requests were streaming?”

7.3 Private customer note (only if asked)
- We support overrides via Helm values. We recommend staying on defaults unless directed by Redwood Support.
- If customer wants to pin/disable profiles:
  - Provide the documented Helm key
  - Ask for runtime version + GPU SKU
  - Encourage capturing effective config dump from the runtime


8) “Known issues / sharp edges” callouts (keep current)
- H100: tail latency regression risk when prefill/decode fairness is too aggressive under mixed streaming workloads (see fix PR-22033).
- L40S: long-context + high concurrency can trigger KV-cache pressure; guardrails should prevent OOM but may reduce throughput.
- B200: limited fleet access; experimental profile must remain gated; explicit disable in specific pools may be required (see hotfix PR-22059 precedent).


9) Open items (as of last edit)

[ ] Sean: confirm pager routing + oncall runbook step-by-step for disable/profile pin
[ ] Connor: confirm exact runtime release number + backport policy
